subject: POC success criteria & next steps (Tribeca Payments)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Gomez <arielle.gomez@tribeca-payments.com>, Ken Park <ken@tribeca-payments.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: POC success criteria & next steps (Tribeca Payments)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and a proposed plan to get the POC running so we can validate performance and quality against your production workload.

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood Inference as the inference backbone for Tribeca’s Payments QA assistant (live support and post-transaction review).

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (we can iterate):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end inference < 250 ms (target: < 200 ms) for 1-2s prompt sizes.
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/sec with 95% success, burst to 150 req/sec for short periods.
- Cost: average cost/token < $0.0006 (we'll provide tokenized estimates and a cost report).
- Quality: automated-match accuracy >= 95% on labeled closed-case tasks OR semantic-similarity AUC > 0.85; false-positive rate < 5% for blocklist/risk rules.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and graceful fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained.

Suggested 2-week evaluation plan (timeline):
- Setup (Days 0-2): creds, endpoints, sample schema, share evaluation doc.
- Data ingest & harness (Days 3-4): you provide sample dataset + test harness; Redwood helps with connector and example prompts.
- Load & quality testing (Days 5-11): run steady-state and burst profiles; collect logs, latency, token usage, and quality metrics.
- Wrap & review (Days 12-13): joint results session, next-step decision.

Ownership / asks:
- Tribeca: provide representative dataset (anonymized) + integration point and test harness by Wed Feb 18.
- Redwood: Marissa (owner) for PM coordination, Jordan (SE) for integration and tuning, Vivek for performance tuning and batch/caching config.

Immediate next steps:
- Please confirm dataset availability date and whether Feb 22 start works for you.
- I'll create a mutual action plan and calendar invite for kickoff.

Attachments: redwood-poc-mop.pdf (sample plan), tribeca-eval-plan.xlsx (evaluation template).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Arielle Gomez <arielle.gomez@tribeca-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ken Park <ken@tribeca-payments.com>, SaaSOps <saasops@tribeca-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Tribeca Payments)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with our internal goals. A few quick notes:

- Dataset: our data team needs until Thu Feb 19 to sanitize and export the representative cases (anonymized). We can deliver the test harness (CSV + some JSON payloads) at the same time.
- Start date: given dataset availability, would you be open to starting on Mon Feb 22 instead of Feb 18?
- Latency: we can accept p95 up to 300 ms during initial tuning; our product lead would like to see a path to <200 ms for production.
- Cost: please clarify what you include in the token count (input vs. output, tokenizer used). We also need a short doc on how you instrument cost during the POC so we can model run-rate.

If you can send the mutual action plan and a kickoff invite for Feb 22, that works for us.

—Arielle
Arielle Gomez
Product Manager, Tribeca Payments
arielle.gomez@tribeca-payments.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Gomez <arielle.gomez@tribeca-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & next steps (Tribeca Payments)

Quick tech clarifications from the SE side — good questions, Arielle.

1) Token accounting:
- We count tokens using the BPE tokenizer we use in the runtime (tiktoken-compatible). Cost report will break down input vs. output tokens and show per-request totals.

2) Latency measurement:
- Our p95 includes end-to-end server processing time (inference only) and the gateway hop; it does not include client-side network outside of Redwood. For the POC we can run a small agent inside your VPC to measure full client-to-response latency if you want exact external numbers.

3) Throughput & test profile:
- Suggested steady-state: 50 req/s for 30 min windows; burst: 150 req/s for 2 min.
- Attached a minimal load test config (load-test-config.yaml) with the exact endpoints and headers we will use.

4) Cost instrumentation:
- We'll provide a per-request token CSV and an aggregate cost dashboard daily. For forecasting, we can extrapolate from the sample run.

One more question: do you want the POC on Hosted Redwood (fastest to get started) or a Private deployment? Hosted is fine for discovery — we can discuss Dedicated capacity for production.

Attaching load-test-config.yaml.

—Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
